title: A trial releases an untested assumption
meaning: A practical trial can renew your shared view by revealing an inaccurate assumption and making changing conditions easier to account for.
text: Changing one sample can sometimes leave a familiar cause unable to explain the result. The Empress in the physical position of Ajna suggests making trials and observing what happens. The Tower in energy supports a constructive search for an unreliable foundation: noticing an assumption that fails examination and releasing the question from it. The Wheel of Fortune in emotions experiences the picture’s movement. Losing an answer that once guided discussion may feel alternately interesting and unfamiliar as other connections become possible for you both.

For example, you try to understand why baking together keeps producing more than expected. A trial arrangement shows that one recipe calls a single piece a portion while another means several pieces. **Examining a foundation lets you see a changing result differently.** You stop explaining the difference solely through the size of the tin. Specific quantities can now be compared. The shift may feel surprising and enlivening: you see which part of the earlier account was simply an unnoticed assumption about a word.

The difficulty is looking for the same concealed mistake in every subsequent difference. Any changed result starts promising another revelation. Your wish to release unreliable foundations remains useful when examination has a particular subject. Sometimes conditions simply differ; your shared view can recognise that while preserving what you already understand and maintaining interest in actual experience.
